text:
Maria: Heads-up — ops flagged a backend degradation that's affecting a subset of hosted customers. Need to align on status page wording + timing for email and social. Who's available?
Sam: I just created the incident, INC-2026-03-21-1. Root cause looks like a cache invalidation bug on routing layer. Confirmed impact: elevated errors and longer tail latency for ~7% of requests.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-03-21-1 created by Sam. Severity: P2. Links: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-03-21-1
Jake: Thanks — recommend: immediate minimal status page entry + a short customer email in 30 minutes acknowledging we see it and are working on it. Avoid speculative root cause in external comms. Keep it calm. :white_check_mark:
Lina: Agreed. For messaging, we should include mitigation steps customers can take (e.g., retry/backoff), and which services are unaffected. Also flag high-touch accounts for AE outreach.
Maria: Draft status page copy suggestion below — please edit:```We are currently investigating elevated error rates affecting a subset of API requests. Our engineers are actively investigating and working on a fix. We will provide updates within 30 minutes. If you are experiencing significant impact, please contact support or your AE.```
Sam: Good. Add a line about a mitigation workaround for some users: `If you use long-lived streaming sessions, restarting the session may restore normal behavior.`
Jake: Updated draft for external email (short):```Subject: We’re investigating intermittent API errorsWe’re investigating intermittent errors impacting a subset of API requests. Our team is working on a fix and will update you within 30 minutes. If you’re seeing production impact, reply to this email or open a ticket at support.redwood.ai.```
Maria: Timing decision: post status page now + send email in 30 minutes (unless fixed). Social hold until resolution. Agree?
Lina: Hold social. Also prepare a short post-incident FAQ for docs and support KB so tickets have consistent answers. I can draft.
Jake: I'll own the status page update and the email send. Sam — can you add a one-line internal update to #incidents when we have a mitigation so we can decide to escalate outbound?
Sam: Yep. I’ll post updates every 15 minutes and ping here for any copy changes. First update: workaround identified for some streaming sessions, engineers rolling out a hotfix.
Maria: Great — I'll create a short checklist for this thread: 1) Jake posts status page (now) 2) Maria to approve final email copy (in 20m) 3) Send email in 30m if not resolved 4) Lina drafts FAQ 5) AE team gets list of affected high-touch customers (Ops to provide) 6) Postmortem + comms post after RCA.
Jake: Status page live with Maria's draft. Link: https://status.redwood.ai/incident/INC-2026-03-21-1 — I included the mitigation note. :rocket:
Maria: Thanks — approving email draft now. If fix lands before 30m we'll send an update instead of the mitigation email.
incident-bot: INC-2026-03-21-1 status changed: investigating -> identifying (1711004234)
Sam: Hotfix deployed to 60% of nodes — errors dropping. Will monitor for 10m then promote globally.
Lina: Drafted the FAQ and support snippets, pasted here:```Q: What happened?A: A routing cache invalidation caused transient errors for a subset of requests. We have deployed a fix and are monitoring.Q: Is my data safe?A: Yes. This was an availability issue; no data loss or leakage.```
Jake: If fix fully validates, send a follow-up email with root cause summary and links to postmortem within 24 hours. We should pre-approve the root-cause wording with incident owners before sending.
Maria: Agree. Sam — please flag when you declare resolved so we can schedule the resolution email and social debrief.
Sam: Will do. Declared resolved at 1711006000. Posting RCA draft in #postmortems in 2h.
Maria: Nice work team. Quick retrospective — the pre-written incident templates helped speed comms. We should add the short streaming-session workaround to the incident templates. :+1:
